problem:
The displacement $s$ (in meters) relative to a fixed origin $O$ of a particle moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis is given by the equation $s(t)=\frac{{2}^{t}}{{2}^{t}+1}$, where $t$ is the time, measured in seconds. Find the position ${s}_{0}$ and velocity ${v}_{0}$ of the particle at the initial moment of time $t=0\,\text{s}.$

${s}_{0}=$
{{field-1}}$\text{m}\,\text{and}\,$

${v}_{0}=$

feedback.problem:
The position $x$ of a particle at time $t$ is given by 

$$
x(t)=16\sqrt{t}-{t}^{4},\,t\ge 0.
$$

Calculate the velocity at time $t=1.$

$v(1)=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
The velocity is the derivative of the position function $x(t)$ with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(16\sqrt{t}-{t}^{4}) \\  & =\frac{16}{2\sqrt{t}}-4{t}^{3} \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{t}}-4{t}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the velocity at $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the velocity function above:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{1}}-4({1}^{3}) \\  & =8-4 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$
